key_insight: Physics residuals are highly effective as a trust signal for CFD predictions, but they are unreliable as a direct correction objective; a learned self-corrector is needed to actually improve the flow field.
engineering_relevance: This enables CFD surrogates to self-audit their outputs, flag low-trust cases, and provide calibrated uncertainty bands for safer deployment in engineering workflows.
method: Compute the discretized steady-RANS residual of each neural CFD prediction as a physics-based trust score.
Add split-conformal calibration and deep-ensemble uncertainty to produce input-adaptive prediction bands with target coverage.
Train a supervised deep-equilibrium corrector to refine the predicted velocity and pressure fields toward ground truth.
evidence_signal: Across multiple backbones and datasets, residual rank correlation with field error is consistently positive (e.g., Transolver 0.625, MeshGraphNet 0.851) and conformal coverage matches the 0.90 target at 0.902.
watch_item: The correction benefit is backbone-dependent, and conformal coverage guarantees only hold under exchangeability assumptions.
paper_title: NeuroForge: A Self-Correcting, Geometry-Native Neural CFD Engine with Calibrated Physics-Residual Trust
